1	# Notes
2	
3	See [design.md](../crates/actor-x1/notes/design.md)
4	
5	
6	## jj tips
7	
8	For users new to jj see [jj-tips.md](jj-tips.md).
9	
10	```
11	## Chores format
12	
13	Filename: "chores-XX.md"
14	example: chores-01.md
15	
16	Format of section labels: "## <short description> (X.Y.Z)"
17	example: "## Topic format description (0.1.0)"
18	
19	Example chore file:
20	```
21	# Chores-01.md
22	 
23	General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
24	more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
25	how and why of a particular chore.
26	
27	## Do something (1.3.1)
28	
29	Describe something
30	```
31	
32	## Versioning during development
33	
34	This is using jujustiu, jj + git and we'll see how it goes. Below is my
35	git workflow, jj will be different but we'll have to discover that as
36	we go.
37	
38	Every plan must start with a version bump. Choose the approach based on scope:
39	
40	- **Single-step** (recommended for mechanical/focused changes): bump directly to
41	  `X.Y.Z`, implement in one commit. Simpler history.
42	- **Multi-step** (for exploratory/large changes): bump to `X.Y.Z-devN`, implement
43	  across multiple commits, final commit removes `-devN`.
44	
45	The plan should recommend one approach and get user approval before starting.
46	
47	For multi-step:
48	1. Bump version to `X.Y.Z-devN` with a plan and commit as a chore marker
49	2. Implement in one or more `-devN` commits (bump N as needed)
50	3. Final commit removes `-devN`, updates todo/chores — this is the "done" marker
51	
52	The final release commit (without `-devN`) signals completion rather than amending
53	prior commits. This keeps the git history readable and makes it easy to see which
54	commits were exploratory vs final.
55	
56	## Todo format
57	
58	Todo.md contains two main sections "Todo" and "Done" each item is a
59	short explanations of a tasks and links to more details using 1 or more
60	references.
61	
62	Multiple references must be separated: `[2],[3]` not `[2,3]` or `[2][3]`.
63	In markdown, `[2,3]` is a single ref key (won't resolve) and `[2][3]`
64	is parsed as display text `2` with ref key `3` (so `[2]` won't resolve).
65	
66	Examples:
67	
68	# Todo
69	
70	- Add new feature X [details](chores-01.md#feature-x)
71	- Fix bug Y [1]
72	
73	# Done
74	
75	- Fixed issue Z [2],[3]
76	
77	[1]: chores-01bugs.md#bug-y

1	# Chores-03.md
2	
3	Chores for the `0.6.0` ladder onward.
4	
5	## RuntimeZC lifecycle: startup / run / stop — plan marker (0.6.0-0)
6	
7	Plan marker for the `0.6.0` multi-step ladder. Splits the
8	runtime's all-in-one `run` / `run_probed` into a caller-
9	orchestrated lifecycle (`startup` / `Handle::run` /
10	`Handle::stop`). Probe support leaves the runtime entirely;
11	re-enters later via `TProbe::Counter` or an actor-wrapper
12	trait (out of scope for this ladder). `stop` is the
13	explicit graceful primitive, matching the post-`0.6.0`
14	typed-message-to-runtime story.
15	
16	### Shape
17	
18	```
19	let handle = rt.startup(&mut mgr, initial, pin_cores);
20	handle.run(duration);        // optional, repeatable
21	let total = handle.stop();   // u64 aggregate; sends Shutdown
22	```
23	
24	### Multi-step ladder
25	
26	(Revised mid-flight after `0.6.0-1`. Original ladder had
27	three sub-steps; expanded to five to make the trait
28	introduction and amortized-bench work explicit. Revised
29	again after `0.6.0-2` to insert the shared-`report`-module
30	side-refactor as `0.6.0-3`, shifting the lifecycle work
31	that was -3/-4/-5 to -4/-5/-6.)
32	
33	- `0.6.0-0` — plan marker (this section + version bump).
34	- `0.6.0-1` — `Handle` + `RuntimeZC::startup` /
35	  `Handle::run` / `Handle::stop`; tests updated. Existing
36	  `run` / `run_probed` stay alongside (additive step).
37	- `0.6.0-2` — Migrate `goalzc` bin and `goalzc-crit` bench
38	  to the lifecycle API. New `Handle::reset_count` (sends
39	  `ClearProbe`; each actor thread zeros its per-thread
40	  count on receipt). `--warmup` restored on `goalzc` and
41	  in `goalzc-crit`'s warmup → measurement split. `goalzc`
42	  loses its band-table (no probing); keeps the msg/s line
43	  as a smoke generator.
44	- `0.6.0-3` — Shared `actor_x1::report` module. Extracts
45	  the bin-prelude helpers duplicated across `goal1` /
46	  `goal2` / `goalzc` (parser, banner, apparatus line,
47	  pinning line) into a single home so the upcoming
48	  probing-re-enters work (post-`0.6.0`, when a probed
49	  `goalzc_probed` bin lands on the wrapper-trait probe
50	  path) has a clean shared surface to call into instead
51	  of yet another copy.
52	- `0.6.0-4` — `Handle::query_count` via signal-and-reply
53	  (oneshot per thread). `goalzc-crit` goes amortized:
54	  `startup` once / `reset_count → run(duration) →
55	  query_count` per criterion sample. Reports the new
56	  amortized number; bench-vs-bin gap collapses (or
57	  doesn't, and we learn something).
58	- `0.6.0-5` — Introduce `Runtime` trait. `RuntimeZC` impls
59	  it. `goalzc` / `goalzc-crit` / tests reach through the
60	  trait, not the concrete type. `SignalZC::ClearProbe`
61	  renamed to `ClearCount` (probe is gone).
62	- `0.6.0-6` — Remove legacy `run` / `run_probed` /
63	  `actor_loop_probed`. Runtime is probe-free +
64	  lifecycle-only.
65	- `0.6.0` — close.
66	
67	### Decisions locked in
68	
69	- **Counter**: per-thread local `u64`, no atomics. Returned
70	  via `JoinHandle` at `stop`. `stop -> u64` aggregate. KIS;
71	  per-actor breakdown is a future `TProbe::Counter`
72	  concern.
73	- **`Handle::run(duration) -> ()`** — just sleeps for the
74	  run window. Counts not readable mid-flight by design.
75	- **`Handle::Drop`** calls `stop` if forgotten; result is
76	  discarded. Join errors are swallowed (drop must not
77	  panic-during-drop).
78	- **Probing leaves the runtime.** `goalzc`'s band-table
79	  goes with it. Probe re-introduction is post-`0.6.0`
80	  work, via `TProbe::Counter` or an actor-wrapper trait.
81	- **`Runtime` trait** introduced in `0.6.0-4`. Consumers
82	  reach through the trait so the post-`0.6.0`
83	  ActorManager-driven graceful shutdown work has a clean
84	  seam to drop into.
85	
86	### Defaults that aren't yet locked
87	
88	- `Handle::pool()` accessor so the caller can inject ad-hoc
89	  messages post-startup. Default yes; revisit during
90	  `0.6.0-1` if the API gets ugly.
91	
92	### Naming: teardown → stop
93	
94	The `0.5.0` close section's "What's next" pointer used
95	the name `teardown` for the lifecycle's shutdown
96	primitive. During the `0.6.0-0` planning round the name
97	settled on `stop` — matches the post-`0.6.0` typed-
98	message-to-runtime story. The chores-02 mention of
99	`teardown` is historical (accurate to the moment it was
100	written, pre-rename) and is left in place per the same
101	precedent `0.5.1` set with `run_no_probe → run`.
102	
103	## Handle + RuntimeZC::startup / Handle::run / Handle::stop (0.6.0-1)
104	
105	Adds the lifecycle API alongside the existing all-in-one
106	`run` / `run_probed`. Caller drives the actor mesh through
107	[`startup`] → [`Handle::run`] (any number of windows) →
108	[`Handle::stop`] (returns the aggregate `u64` count and
109	joins). Probe-free; counts come from per-thread local
110	`u64`s summed via `JoinHandle` at `stop`. The all-in-one
111	paths still work (refactored to share spawn / seed logic);
112	they go away in `0.6.0-3`.
113	
114	- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-0` → `0.6.0-1`.
115	- `crates/actor-x1/src/runtime_zc.rs`:
116	  - New private `RuntimeZC::spawn_and_seed<R>` extracts
117	    the spawn + channel-wire + initial-message-deliver
118	    logic shared by the all-in-one `run_inner` and the
119	    new `startup`. `run_inner` is now a thin wrapper that
120	    composes `spawn_and_seed` with the warmup / clear /
121	    measurement / shutdown / join sequence.
122	  - New `pub fn RuntimeZC::startup(mgr, initial, pin) ->
123	    Handle<S>` returns a live handle to the actor mesh.
124	  - New `pub struct Handle<S = MutexLifo>` with
125	    `pub fn run(&self, window: Duration)` (just sleeps),
126	    `pub fn pool(&self) -> &Pool<S>` (caller injection /
127	    inspection), `pub fn stop(self) -> u64` (sends
128	    `Shutdown`, joins, sums per-thread counts — panics
129	    on actor panic).
130	  - `impl Drop for Handle` performs silent graceful
131	    shutdown if `stop` was not called: sends `Shutdown`,
132	    joins, swallows panics and counts. Drop must not
133	    panic-during-drop.
134	  - Module-level docstring: rewritten around the two API
135	    styles (Lifecycle preferred / All-in-one legacy).
136	  - Tests: `lifecycle_round_trip_returns_total`,
137	    `lifecycle_multiple_run_windows_accumulate`,
138	    `lifecycle_handle_pool_accessor`,
139	    `lifecycle_handle_drop_shuts_down_cleanly`. All four
140	    validate the drain invariant (`pool.free_len() ==
141	    pool.size()` after the handle goes away).
142	- `notes/todo.md`: mark `0.6.0-1` done.
143	- `notes/chores-03.md`: this section.
144	
145	### Design notes
146	
147	- **`Handle`'s state**: `senders: Option<Vec<Sender<...>>>`
148	  and `handles: Option<Vec<JoinHandle<u64>>>`. `stop`
149	  consumes via `take()`; `Drop` checks the same `Option`s
150	  and runs the silent path only if `stop` didn't.
151	  Simpler than typestate; KIS.
152	- **Counter aggregation**: each actor thread keeps a
153	  local `u64`, returned via `JoinHandle::Output`. `stop`
154	  sums them with `saturating_add`. No atomics in the hot
155	  path.
156	- **No mid-flight count read**: `Handle::run(window)`
157	  returns `()`. Per-window deltas would require atomics
158	  or signal-and-reply; both rejected as not worth the
159	  complexity at the user's KIS preference.
160	- **`spawn_and_seed` lives on `RuntimeZC`**, not as a
161	  free function, because it uses `self.pool` and is the
162	  natural place for the shared logic. Generic over `R`
163	  so both probe-free and probed actor loops share it.
164	- **Pool sizing in tests**: the lifecycle tests use the
165	  `Pool::new(., 4)` ping-pong-steady-state recommendation
166	  from the `0.5.0` chores (4 buffers covers 2 in flight
167	  + 2 headroom). One initial test draft used the
168	  capacity-2 pool from a non-running test and hit
169	  `NoMsgs` under traffic; standardized on 4.
170	
171	### What's not in 0.6.0-1
172	
173	- `goalzc` and `goalzc-crit` still call the legacy
174	  `run_probed` / `run` paths. `0.6.0-2` migrates them.
175	- Legacy `RuntimeZC::run` / `run_probed` /
176	  `actor_loop_probed` / the `ClearProbe` signal path stay
177	  untouched for now. `0.6.0-3` removes them.
178	
179	## Migrate goalzc bin and goalzc-crit bench to lifecycle (0.6.0-2)
180	
181	`goalzc` and `goalzc-crit` move off the legacy all-in-one
182	`RuntimeZC::run_probed` / `run` to the lifecycle API
183	(`startup` / `Handle::run` / `Handle::stop`). Adds
184	`Handle::reset_count` so the warmup → measurement
185	boundary can zero per-thread counts mid-flight. `goalzc`
186	loses its band-table report (no probing in the runtime;
187	re-enters post-`0.6.0`) and becomes a smoke generator
188	that prints msg/s. `goalzc-crit` keeps its
189	cycle-per-sample shape, just through the new API.
190	
191	- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-1` → `0.6.0-2`.
192	- `crates/actor-x1/src/runtime_zc.rs`:
193	  - New `pub fn Handle::reset_count(&self)` sends
194	    `SignalZC::ClearProbe` to every actor thread; on
195	    receipt each thread zeros its per-thread count.
196	    Best-effort: if a thread already exited, the send
197	    silently fails (its count is already captured in
198	    its `JoinHandle::Output`).
199	  - New test `lifecycle_reset_count_runs_clean` exercises
200	    `startup → run → reset_count → run → stop`; asserts
201	    nonzero post-reset total + drain invariant.
202	- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goalzc.rs`:
203	  - CLI: drop `--ticks` (`-t`), `--decimals` (`-d`).
204	    Keep `duration_s` (positional), `--warmup` (`-w`,
205	    default 0.5), `--size` (`-s`), `--pin` (`-p`).
206	  - Drop the apparatus calibration call and the
207	    per-thread `tprobe` band-table report.
208	  - Use `rt.startup` → `handle.run(warmup)` →
209	    `handle.reset_count()` → `handle.run(measurement)`
210	    → `handle.stop` to drive the actors.
211	  - Output: version banner, throughput line
212	    (`goalzc: <count> messages in <Ds> (<R> M msg/s,
213	    <N> actors, size=<S> B)`), and `pinning:` line if
214	    `--pin` was set. No `apparatus:` line, no band
215	    table.
216	  - Imports trimmed: `tprobe::{fmt_commas, pin}` only
217	    (was `tprobe::{self as perf, fmt_commas, pin,
218	    ticks}` plus probe-side report calls).
219	  - `n_actors = 2` hardcoded since the bin always
220	    creates two actors (assertion already pins
221	    `(a_id, b_id) == (0, 1)`).
222	- `crates/actor-x1/benches/goalzc-crit.rs`:
223	  - Switch `rt.run` → `rt.startup` /
224	    `handle.run(warmup)` / `handle.reset_count()` /
225	    `handle.run(measurement)` / `handle.stop`.
226	  - Keep the prior 50 ms warmup + 100 ms measurement
227	    split. `per_msg_ns = measurement / measurement_count`
228	    (post-reset only).
229	  - Module docstring rewritten around the lifecycle
230	    API and the smoke-bench scope.
231	- `notes/todo.md`: mark `0.6.0-2` done.
232	- `notes/chores-03.md`: this section.
233	
234	### Smoke results (`--size 64`, unpinned)
235	
236	- `goalzc-crit/pingpong`: ~260 K msg/s (criterion CI
237	  [250, 269] K elem/s; "Performance has improved",
238	  p=0.04 vs the pre-restoration single-window baseline
239	  at ~233 K). Restoring `--warmup` (50 ms) before the
240	  100 ms measurement window — and using `reset_count`
241	  to drop the warmup count — exposes the steady-state
242	  rate.
243	- `goalzc 10 -w 3`: ~293 K msg/s. Modest improvement vs
244	  the <USER_2>`0.6.0` probed path (~281 K); the bot thinks
245	  this is the probe overhead leaving the hot loop —
246	  ~5.8 ns / dispatch ≈ 0.17% of the per-message cost —
247	  near the edge of run-to-run noise but pointing the
248	  right way.
249	- Bench-vs-bin ratio: 260 / 293 ≈ 0.89, narrower than
250	  the pre-restoration 232 / 281 ≈ 0.83. The remaining
251	  11% is the per-sample fresh-`startup` cost in the
252	  bench; `0.6.0-3`'s `startup`-once + `query_count`
253	  amortization aims at that.
254	
255	### CLI breaking change in 0.6.0-2
256	
257	`goalzc`'s `--ticks` / `--decimals` flags are gone (band-
258	table is gone). `--warmup` is preserved with the same
259	semantics it had <USER_2>`0.6.0`: warmup window precedes
260	measurement, and reported throughput reflects only the
261	measurement window.
262	
263	### Naming: window → duration
264	
265	`Handle::run`'s parameter `window: Duration` renamed to
266	`duration: Duration` — matches `std::thread::sleep(dur)`
267	and `tokio::time::sleep(duration)` conventions, removes
268	the overloaded "window" reading from the public API. In
269	prose, bare "window" becomes "run window"; "warmup
270	window" / "measurement window" stay as already-qualified
271	compound terms. The `0.6.0-1` chores section above
272	describes the parameter as `window: Duration`, accurate
273	at the time, left in place per the same precedent
274	`0.5.1` set with `run_no_probe → run`.
275	
276	## Shared `report` module: extract bin-prelude helpers (0.6.0-3)
277	
278	Side-refactor inserted into the `0.6.0` ladder between the
279	lifecycle migration (`0.6.0-2`) and the upcoming
280	`query_count` work (`0.6.0-4`). Collapses the prelude
281	helpers that `goal1` / `goal2` / `goalzc` each had a copy
282	of into a single `actor_x1::report` module. No behavior
283	change — output is byte-for-byte identical across all three
284	bins.
285	
286	Motivation:
287	
288	- The bot thinks the post-`0.6.0` probing-re-enters work
289	  (when `goalzc_probed` lands on the wrapper-trait / 
290	  `TProbe::Counter` path) will want the same prelude lines
291	  as `goal1` / `goal2`. Doing the dedup *before* that bin
292	  arrives means one shared surface to call into instead
293	  of a fourth copy.
294	- `goal1` and `goal2` each duplicated the
295	  `parse_non_negative_secs` clap helper, the
296	  `framing / loop_per_iter / per-event` apparatus
297	  printout, and the `pinning:` line; `goalzc` had the
298	  parser and the multi-actor pinning printout.
299	
300	Edits:
301	
302	- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-2` → `0.6.0-3`.
303	- `crates/actor-x1/src/lib.rs`: declare `pub mod report;`.
304	- `crates/actor-x1/src/report.rs`: new module.
305	  - `parse_non_negative_secs(s) -> Result<f64, String>` —
306	    clap `value_parser` for non-negative finite seconds.
307	  - `parse_pin_cores(spec: Option<&str>) -> Vec<usize>` —
308	    `None` → `vec![]`; bad input prints
309	    `error: --pin: <msg>` and exits `2`. Centralizing the
310	    exit here keeps each bin free of duplicated error
311	    handling.
312	  - `print_banner()` — `actor-x1 <version>` one-liner from
313	    this crate's `CARGO_PKG_*`.
314	  - `print_apparatus(&Overhead, inner: u64)` — the
315	    `apparatus: framing=... ; loop_per_iter=... ; per-event
316	    at inner=N = ...` line.
317	  - `print_pinning(&[usize], n_actors: usize)` — multi-actor
318	    `pinning:` line (goal2 / goalzc wording —
319	    `actor<i>→core<n>`).
320	  - `print_pinning_main(Option<usize>)` — single-thread
321	    `pinning:` line (goal1 wording — `main → core <c>`).
322	    Distinct from `print_pinning` because goal1 pins the
323	    main thread itself, not a spawned actor; the prior
324	    output preserved both forms verbatim.
325	- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goal1.rs`: strip duplicated
326	  helpers; call `report::print_banner`,
327	  `report::parse_pin_cores`, `report::print_pinning_main`,
328	  `report::print_apparatus`. `parse_non_negative_secs`
329	  flag bodies now reference `report::parse_non_negative_secs`.
330	  Tprobe import trimmed: `tprobe::{self as perf, fmt_commas,
331	  pin}` (drops `ticks` — the per-event ns conversion lives
332	  in `report` now).
333	- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goal2.rs`: same shape.
334	  `parse_pin_cores` collapses the `match cli.pin.as_deref()
335	  { ... pin::parse_cores ... exit(2) }` block to one line.
336	  Tprobe import trimmed: `tprobe::{self as perf, fmt_commas}`
337	  (drops `pin` and `ticks` — goal2 doesn't pin the main
338	  thread, only spawned actors via the runtime).
339	- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goalzc.rs`: same shape, smaller
340	  surface (no apparatus call; no probing). Local
341	  `parse_positive_size` for `--size` stays in the bin —
342	  only goalzc has a payload-size flag, so it doesn't belong
343	  in the shared module. Tprobe import trimmed: `tprobe::
344	  fmt_commas` (drops `pin` — `parse_pin_cores` covers the
345	  one call site).
346	- `notes/todo.md`: insert `0.6.0-3` done line; renumber the
347	  lifecycle steps that were -3/-4/-5 to -4/-5/-6.
348	- `notes/chores-03.md`: revise the ladder table; this
349	  section.
350	
351	### Why the helpers live in `actor-x1`, not `tprobe`
352	
353	- The formatted lines are *bin prelude*, not perf-library
354	  surface. `tprobe` already owns the data
355	  ([`Overhead`], `ticks_per_ns`, `fmt_commas`); the bins
356	  own the *wording* (column spacing, label choice,
357	  pinning prose). Keeping the wording in `actor-x1` puts
358	  the prose next to the bins that produce it.
359	- A future external consumer of `tprobe` would print the
360	  same numbers in its own house style; promoting our
361	  particular phrasing to `tprobe` would foist our prose
362	  on every downstream <USER_3>
363	
364	### Why two pinning helpers
365	
366	`goal1` pins the main thread itself (single-threaded) and
367	its line says `pinning: main → core <c>`; `goal2` /
368	`goalzc` pin spawned actor threads and their line says
369	`pinning: actor<i>→core<n>`. The two are intentionally
370	worded differently (`main` vs `actor<i>`; spaced `→` vs
371	unspaced `→`). Preserving byte-for-byte output across the
372	refactor meant providing both forms rather than collapsing
373	them.
374	
375	### Bin-output policy left in the bins
376	
377	- `--ticks` / `--decimals` flags (probed bins only).
378	- The per-actor `probe.report(...)` call (each bin chooses
379	  which probes to render).
380	- The throughput line (`goal1: ... messages in ...`) — the
381	  bin name is baked into the format string. Promoting that
382	  to `report::print_throughput(&str, count, dur_s, ...)`
383	  would gain little and lose the literal-grep-ability of
384	  the per-bin line.

3	## Overview
4	
5	Actor-x1 is a system that uses Communicating
6	Sequential Process (CSP) invented by Tony Hoare

10

12	     the runtime providing control and to capture
13	     logs and assists in developing the app

16	     other actors.
17	
18	 - A runtime that drives the system and provides
19	   resources and services for the system
20	   - interfaces between the manager and the application
21	 
22	 - One or more actors running on one or more
23	   threads. Each actor adheres to these
24	   invariants:
25	   - Has on basic entry point; handler()
26	   - The handler() handles one message at a time and
27	     must run to completion as quickly as possible.

32	     messages to communicate with its parent and
33	     other actors as it does its work.

## Handle::query_count + amortized goalzc-crit (0.6.0-4)

Adds the signal-and-reply mid-flight count read so
`goalzc-crit` can amortize bench setup: `startup` once,
warm up once, then per criterion sample just
`reset_count → run(measurement) → query_count`. The
all-in-one `startup` / thread-spawn / `stop` / join cost
that used to live inside `iter_custom` now happens once
per benchmark group.

- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-3` → `0.6.0-4`.
- `crates/actor-x1/src/runtime_zc.rs`:
  - New `SignalZC::QueryCount(Sender<u64>)` variant. On
    receipt, the actor sends its current per-thread `count`
    over the reply channel and continues. Probe state (if
    any, on the legacy probed loop) is untouched.
  - `actor_loop` and `actor_loop_probed` both handle the
    new variant. The probed loop's update is functionally
    dead-on-arrival (legacy paths go away in `0.6.0-6`)
    but keeps the function-pointer signature uniform.
  - New `pub fn Handle::query_count(&self) -> u64`. Builds
    an `mpsc::channel::<u64>()`, sends `QueryCount(tx.clone())`
    to every actor sender, tracks how many sends succeeded,
    drops the original `tx`, and receives exactly that many
    replies. Aggregation uses `saturating_add` (matches
    [`Handle::stop`]).
  - Module docstring: lifecycle bullet extended to mention
    `reset_count` and `query_count`.
  - New tests: `lifecycle_query_count_monotonic`
    (`startup → run → query → run → query → stop`; asserts
    `first > 0`, `second ≥ first`, `total ≥ second`),
    `lifecycle_query_count_after_reset`
    (`startup → run → reset → run → query → stop`; asserts
    `queried > 0` and `total ≥ queried`).
- `crates/actor-x1/benches/goalzc-crit.rs`:
  - Pool / runtime / manager / `startup` moved outside
    `b.iter_custom`. One initial 50 ms warmup happens before
    sampling starts; the handle drops at the end of the
    bench function (silent shutdown).
  - Per `iter_custom` call: `reset_count → run(100 ms) →
    query_count`. Same `per_msg_ns = measurement /
    measurement_count` scaling.
  - `group.measurement_time` reduced 10 s → 6 s. With the
    per-sample overhead gone (~150 ms → ~100 ms), 50 samples
    fit in ~5 s of sampling phase plus criterion's internal
    warmup.
  - Module docstring rewritten around the amortized shape.
- `notes/todo.md`: mark `0.6.0-4` done.
- `notes/chores-03.md`: this section.

### Why best-effort `send` tracking

`Handle::query_count` tracks how many actor sends succeeded
and only `rx.recv`s that many replies. If an actor thread
already exited (channel closed, `send` returns `Err`), its
count is unreachable — but skipping its slot in the recv
loop avoids a deadlock that would otherwise block the
caller forever waiting for a reply that's never coming.
Matches `reset_count`'s best-effort pattern. In practice
the handle is alive (<USER_2>`stop`) so all sends succeed; the
defensive shape is for symmetry.

### Smoke results (`--size 64`, unpinned)

- `goalzc-crit/pingpong` amortized: ~229 K msg/s (criterion
  CI [220, 237] K elem/s; criterion reports "Performance
  has regressed", p < 0.05, throughput change −2.6% to
  −11% vs the `0.6.0-2` non-amortized baseline at ~260 K).
- Direction is opposite to what the chores-03 prediction
  expected — the bench-vs-bin gap *widened*, not collapsed.
  The bot thinks the most likely cause is that the actor
  threads now run continuously for the full ~6 s sampling
  phase (50 samples × ~100 ms back-to-back), where the
  non-amortized variant spun threads up fresh each sample
  with ~50 ms idle between samples. Sustained two-core
  load could be hitting thermal / frequency-boost limits
  that the bursty variant escaped. A pin-to-isolated-cores
  comparison would be the cheap next experiment; not done
  here.
- The regression is an empirical finding worth keeping,
  not a reason to revert: the amortized API is correct,
  the lifecycle surface is the right shape for the post-
  `0.6.0` story, and `query_count` is independently useful
  beyond benches. The bench number is a measurement, not
  a goal.

### CLI / runtime surface impact

- Public lifecycle API gains one method (`Handle::query_count`);
  nothing removed, nothing renamed.
- `SignalZC` gains one private variant — internal only;
  no consumer outside `runtime_zc.rs` touches it.
- No CLI changes."}

2	//!
3	//! See `crates/actor-x1/notes/design.md` for the staged design. Stage 1 provides
4	//! a minimal runtime with two actors that ping-pong an empty
5	//! [`Message`] for a caller-supplied duration; Goal1 runs both
6	//! actors on one thread, Goal2 runs each actor on its own thread.
7	//!
8	//! Public surface today:
9	//! - [`Message`]: the empty unit message Stage 1 actors exchange.
10	//! - [`Actor`]: the single-method actor trait.
11	//! - [`Context`]: the send-side handle passed to each dispatch.
12	//! - [`runtime`]: concrete runtimes (single-thread for Goal1; the
13	//!   multi-thread runtime will land in 0.1.0-3).

15	pub mod actor_manager;
16	pub mod pool;
17	pub mod report;
18	pub mod runtime;
19	pub mod runtime_zc;

21	/// Empty unit-type message exchanged between Stage 1 actors.
22	/// Carries no payload by design — Stage 1's contract is only
23	/// "dispatch happens"; Stage 2 replaces this with a richer type.
24	pub struct Message;
25	
26	/// Actor behavior: handle one [`Message`] at a time, never blocking.
27	///
28	/// The only method is [`Actor::handle_message`]; all outbound
29	/// communication goes through the [`Context`] the runtime supplies.
30	pub trait Actor {
31	    /// Handle a single incoming message. Use `ctx` to emit any

39	/// the (future) multi-thread runtime writes to per-actor channels.

42	    /// `dst_id`. Returns immediately; delivery is the runtime's job.

Before implementing, let me lay out the design choices since the chores entry was high-level:

**Proposed shape**:

1. **Trait name & location**: `pub trait Runtime<S: BufRefStore>` in `runtime_zc.rs`. No naming conflict — legacy types are `SingleThreadRuntime`/`MultiThreadRuntime` (in `runtime.rs`).

2. **Trait surface** (minimal, matches what consumers actually call):
   ```rust
   pub trait Runtime<S: BufRefStore> {
       fn startup(&mut self, mgr: &mut ActorManager<S>, initial: Vec<(u32, PooledMsg<S>)>, pin: &[usize]) -> Handle<S>;
       fn pool(&self) -> &Pool<S>;
   }
   ```
   - `Handle<S>` stays a concrete return type. Making it a trait too adds an associated type with no current consumer needing it — out of scope per VENDOR_A.md "don't design for hypothetical future requirements".
   - `RuntimeZC::new(pool)` stays as an inherent constructor (not a trait method).

3. **Inherent methods**: move `startup` and `pool` to **trait-only** (drop the inherent versions). Consumers `use actor_x1::runtime_zc::Runtime;` to bring them in scope — that's what "reach through the trait" means concretely. Without the import, code won't compile, so the seam is real, not nominal. Legacy `run` / `run_probed` stay inherent (they go in `-6`).

4. **`SignalZC::ClearProbe → ClearCount`** rename — internal only, no external impact.

5. **Touched consumers**: `goalzc.rs`, `goalzc-crit.rs`, `runtime_zc.rs` tests — add `use ... Runtime;` import; behavior unchanged.

Sound right, or do you want a different trait shape (e.g., add a `Handle` trait too, or keep methods inherent + duplicate on the trait)?

1	//! Multi-threaded zerocopy runtime — message-moving
2	//! infrastructure.
3	//!
4	//! Pairs with [`crate::actor_manager`], which owns the actor
5	//! model surface ([`ActorZC`], [`ContextZC`], [`ActorManager`]).
6	//! This module is one consumer of that surface; future
7	//! transports (M:N scheduler, alternative channel types, …)
8	//! would be peers.
9	//!
10	//! Two API styles in this version:
11	//!
12	//! - **Lifecycle (preferred, new in `0.6.0-1`)**: caller
13	//!   composes [`RuntimeZC::startup`] →
14	//!   [`Handle::run`] (any number of run windows) →
15	//!   [`Handle::stop`]. `stop` returns the aggregate `u64`
16	//!   message count across all actor threads. Probe-free;
17	//!   diagnostic instrumentation will re-enter post-`0.6.0`
18	//!   via an actor-wrapper trait or `TProbe::Counter`.
19	//!   [`Handle::reset_count`] zeros per-thread counts mid-
20	//!   flight (warmup → measurement boundary).
21	//!   [`Handle::query_count`] reads the aggregate without
22	//!   stopping (amortize bench setup across samples).
23	//! - **All-in-one (legacy, removed in `0.6.0-3`)**:
24	//!   [`RuntimeZC::run`] (probe-free, returns per-actor
25	//!   counts) and [`RuntimeZC::run_probed`] (probe-
26	//!   instrumented, returns per-actor `(count, TProbe)`).
27	//!   These manage their own warmup → measurement → shutdown
28	//!   internally; the warmup boundary issues `ClearProbe` so
29	//!   counts and the histogram only see steady-state data.
30	//!
31	//! Drain invariant: by the time the join completes, every
32	//! [`PooledMsg`] that was ever in flight has been dropped, so
33	//! `pool.free_len() == pool.size()`. Holds for both API
34	//! styles.

36	use std::sync::mpsc::{self, Receiver, Sender};
37	use std::thread::{self, JoinHandle};
38	use std::time::Duration;

41	use crate::pool::{BufRefStore, MutexLifo, Pool, PoolError, PooledMsg};
42	use tprobe::TProbe;

44	/// Internal channel payload.
45	///
46	/// - `User(msg)` — caller-visible traffic.
47	/// - `ClearProbe` — runtime injects at warmup → measurement
48	///   boundary so the report only sees steady-state data.
49	/// - `QueryCount(reply)` — lifecycle injects on
50	///   [`Handle::query_count`]; actor sends its current per-
51	///   thread count over `reply` and continues running. Probe
52	///   state (if any) is untouched.
53	/// - `Shutdown` — runtime injects after the measurement
54	///   window; actor exits its `recv` loop on receipt.
55	enum SignalZC<S: BufRefStore> {
56	    User(PooledMsg<S>),
57	    ClearProbe,
58	    QueryCount(Sender<u64>),

## Runtime trait + ClearProbe → ClearCount rename (0.6.0-5)

Introduces a `Runtime` trait carrying the lifecycle entry
points (`startup` + `pool`) so post-`0.6.0`
ActorManager-driven graceful-shutdown work has a stable
seam to drop into. `RuntimeZC` impls the trait; the
inherent `startup` / `pool` methods are dropped — consumers
reach through the trait via `use
actor_x1::runtime_zc::Runtime;`. Without the import the
code won't compile, so the seam is real, not nominal.

Also renames `SignalZC::ClearProbe` to `SignalZC::ClearCount`:
the runtime is probe-free since `0.6.0-2`, so the old name
was misleading. Pure internal rename — the enum is private.

- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-4` → `0.6.0-5`.
- `crates/actor-x1/src/runtime_zc.rs`:
  - `pub trait Runtime<S: BufRefStore>` with
    `fn startup(&mut self, &mut ActorManager<S>, Vec<(u32,
    PooledMsg<S>)>, &[usize]) -> Handle<S>` and
    `fn pool(&self) -> &Pool<S>`. Object-safe (`&self` /
    `&mut self`, no generic params on methods).
  - `impl<S: BufRefStore + 'static> Runtime<S> for
    RuntimeZC<S>` — body identical to the prior inherent
    methods.
  - Removed the inherent `RuntimeZC::startup` and
    `RuntimeZC::pool` methods. `RuntimeZC::new` stays
    inherent (constructor, not on the trait).
  - `SignalZC::ClearProbe` → `SignalZC::ClearCount`
    (variant rename + all `tx.send(SignalZC::ClearProbe)`
    /  pattern-match arms updated). Doc comments
    referencing the old name updated; the rename history
    is recorded on the variant's own doc.
  - Module docstring: lifecycle bullet now points to
    `Runtime::startup` and documents the trait-import
    requirement.
- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goalzc.rs`: `use
  actor_x1::runtime_zc::{Runtime, RuntimeZC};` (added
  `Runtime`). No other change — `rt.startup(...)` now
  resolves through the trait impl.
- `crates/actor-x1/benches/goalzc-crit.rs`: same import
  change. No other change.
- `notes/todo.md`: mark `0.6.0-5` done.
- `notes/chores-03.md`: this section.

### Why drop the inherent methods rather than keep both

Keeping both inherent and trait methods with the same name
makes `rt.startup(...)` resolve to the inherent method
*even when the trait is in scope* (Rust prefers inherent
over trait when both exist). That defeats the purpose of
"consumers reach through the trait" — the trait would
become a passive descriptor rather than the live dispatch
path. Dropping the inherent versions forces the trait
import, which is exactly the seam future work needs.

### Why `Handle` stays a concrete return type

Making `Handle` a trait too (with an associated `type
Handle: Handle<S>` on `Runtime`) would let the runtime
return its own handle type. But: no current or
short-horizon consumer needs that flexibility — every
zerocopy runtime in the codebase or planned for `0.6.x`
will use the same per-thread-counter handle shape. Per
VENDOR_A.md: don't design for hypothetical future
requirements. If a second handle shape arrives, lift to
an associated type then.

### Why `Runtime`, not `RuntimeApi` / `Lifecycle` / etc.

- The trait is the canonical lifecycle surface for the
  zerocopy runtime family; `Runtime` reads at the call
  site (`use ...::Runtime; rt.startup(...)`) as exactly
  what it is.
- No collision with the legacy `runtime` module — that
  module's types are `SingleThreadRuntime` and
  `MultiThreadRuntime`, never bare `Runtime`. The
  legacy types will eventually be replaced by their
  zerocopy successors anyway (post-`0.6.0` cleanup).
- `RuntimeApi` adds three syllables without resolving any
  ambiguity. `Lifecycle` describes the methods but loses
  "this is a runtime."

### Smoke validation

- `cargo test`: 35 passed (actor-x1) + 18 passed (tprobe).
  Lifecycle tests still exercise `startup` /
  `reset_count` / `query_count` / `stop`, now dispatched
  through the trait impl.
- `cargo run --release --bin goalzc -- 1 -w 0.3`:
  234 K msg/s at 64 B unpinned. Normal range for the
  amortized goalzc path; trait extraction is dispatch-
  equivalent to the prior inherent methods (single static
  call site → monomorphized impl method).
- `goalzc-crit` not re-run for `0.6.0-5` — no codegen
  difference expected vs `0.6.0-4`."}

1	//! Multi-threaded zerocopy runtime — message-moving
2	//! infrastructure.
3	//!
4	//! Pairs with [`crate::actor_manager`], which owns the actor
5	//! model surface ([`ActorZC`], [`ContextZC`], [`ActorManager`]).
6	//! This module is one consumer of that surface; future
7	//! transports (M:N scheduler, alternative channel types, …)
8	//! would be peers.
9	//!
10	//! Two API styles in this version:
11	//!
12	//! - **Lifecycle (preferred, new in `0.6.0-1`)**: caller
13	//!   composes [`Runtime::startup`] →
14	//!   [`Handle::run`] (any number of run windows) →
15	//!   [`Handle::stop`]. `stop` returns the aggregate `u64`
16	//!   message count across all actor threads. Probe-free;
17	//!   diagnostic instrumentation will re-enter post-`0.6.0`
18	//!   via an actor-wrapper trait or `TProbe::Counter`.
19	//!   [`Handle::reset_count`] zeros per-thread counts mid-
20	//!   flight (warmup → measurement boundary).
21	//!   [`Handle::query_count`] reads the aggregate without
22	//!   stopping (amortize bench setup across samples).
23	//!   Consumers reach through the [`Runtime`] trait (in
24	//!   scope via `use actor_x1::runtime_zc::Runtime;`) — the
25	//!   inherent `startup` / `pool` methods on [`RuntimeZC`]
26	//!   were removed in `0.6.0-5`.
27	//! - **All-in-one (legacy, removed in `0.6.0-6`)**:
28	//!   [`RuntimeZC::run`] (probe-free, returns per-actor
29	//!   counts) and [`RuntimeZC::run_probed`] (probe-
30	//!   instrumented, returns per-actor `(count, TProbe)`).
31	//!   These manage their own warmup → measurement → shutdown
32	//!   internally; the warmup boundary issues `ClearCount` so
33	//!   counts and the histogram only see steady-state data.
34	//!
35	//! Drain invariant: by the time the join completes, every
36	//! [`PooledMsg`] that was ever in flight has been dropped, so
37	//! `pool.free_len() == pool.size()`. Holds for both API
38	//! styles.
39	
40	use std::sync::mpsc::{self, Receiver, Sender};
41	use std::thread::{self, JoinHandle};
42	use std::time::Duration;
43	
44	use crate::actor_manager::{ActorManager, ActorZC, ContextZC};
45	use crate::pool::{BufRefStore, MutexLifo, Pool, PoolError, PooledMsg};
46	use tprobe::TProbe;

48	/// Internal channel payload.
49	///
50	/// - `User(msg)` — caller-visible traffic.
51	/// - `ClearCount` — runtime / [`Handle::reset_count`] injects
52	///   at the warmup → measurement boundary so the count and
53	///   any probe state only see steady-state data. Renamed
54	///   from `ClearProbe` in `0.6.0-5` (the runtime is probe-
55	///   free; the legacy probed loop still clears its probe
56	///   on the same signal until it's removed in `0.6.0-6`).
57	/// - `QueryCount(reply)` — lifecycle injects on
58	///   [`Handle::query_count`]; actor sends its current per-
59	///   thread count over `reply` and continues running. Probe
60	///   state (if any) is untouched.
61	/// - `Shutdown` — runtime injects after the measurement
62	///   window; actor exits its `recv` loop on receipt.
63	enum SignalZC<S: BufRefStore> {
64	    User(PooledMsg<S>),
65	    ClearCount,
66	    QueryCount(Sender<u64>),
67	    Shutdown,
68	}
69	
70	/// Multi-threaded zerocopy runtime — message-moving
71	/// infrastructure.
72	///
73	/// - Owns the [`Pool<S>`] (cloned cheaply to each actor
74	///   thread).
75	/// - Spawns threads, wires channels, runs the warmup /
76	///   measure / shutdown lifecycle.
77	/// - Knows nothing about "seeds", named lookups, or what's
78	///   being measured. Initial messages come in as a parameter
79	///   to `run` and are delivered after spawn / before warmup.
80	/// - Generic over the store backend `S` so concurrency
81	///   strategies can be swapped and benchmarked. Default
82	///   [`MutexLifo`].
83	pub struct RuntimeZC<S: BufRefStore = MutexLifo> {
84	    pool: Pool<S>,
85	}

87	impl<S: BufRefStore + 'static> RuntimeZC<S> {
88	    /// Build a runtime that draws buffers from `pool`.
89	    ///
90	    /// - The runtime stores a cheap `Arc` clone; the caller

93	    /// - Constructor is inherent (not on [`Runtime`]); the

96	        Self { pool }
97	    }

101	    ///
102	    /// - `initial_messages` are delivered after thread spawn,
103	    ///   before warmup.

108	    ///   free path on the runtime from the start avoids the
109	    ///   trap of a bench that secretly measures `work + tprobe`.
110	    pub fn run(
111	        &mut self,
112	        mgr: &mut ActorManager<S>,
113	        initial_messages: Vec<(u32, PooledMsg<S>)>,
114	        warmup: Duration,
115	        measurement: Duration,
116	        pin_cores: &[usize],
117	    ) -> Vec<u64> {
118	        self.run_inner(
119	            mgr,
120	            initial_messages,
121	            warmup,
122	            measurement,
123	            pin_cores,
124	            actor_loop::<S>,
125	        )
126	    }

129	    /// per-message [`TProbe`] in the hot loop.
130	    ///
131	    /// - Each actor thread owns a `TProbe` recording per-
132	    ///   `handle_message` latency at `inner=1`.
133	    /// - Returns `(count, probe)` per actor in id order.
134	    /// - Used by the `goalzc` binary's diagnostic report.
135	    ///   Avoid in benches: probe overhead contaminates the
136	    ///   measurement.
137	    pub fn run_probed(
138	        &mut self,
139	        mgr: &mut ActorManager<S>,
140	        initial_messages: Vec<(u32, PooledMsg<S>)>,
141	        warmup: Duration,
142	        measurement: Duration,
143	        pin_cores: &[usize],
144	    ) -> Vec<(u64, TProbe)> {
145	        self.run_inner(
146	            mgr,
147	            initial_messages,
148	            warmup,
149	            measurement,
150	            pin_cores,
151	            actor_loop_probed::<S>,
152	        )
153	    }
154	
155	    /// Spawn actor threads and deliver initial messages.
156	    /// Shared startup logic for [`RuntimeZC::run`] /
157	    /// [`RuntimeZC::run_probed`] (legacy all-in-one) and
158	    /// [`Runtime::startup`] (lifecycle).
159	    ///
160	    /// - Drains the manager's actors via
161	    ///   [`ActorManager::take_actors`].
162	    /// - Builds one `mpsc` channel per actor; spawns one
163	    ///   thread per actor running `actor_loop`, optionally
164	    ///   pinned via `pin_cores[id % pin_cores.len()]`.
165	    /// - Sends `initial_messages` over the per-actor
166	    ///   senders before returning.
167	    /// - Returns the senders (for `ClearCount` / `Shutdown`
168	    ///   signaling) and join handles (for the eventual join).
169	    fn spawn_and_seed<R: Send + 'static>(
170	        &self,
171	        mgr: &mut ActorManager<S>,
172	        initial_messages: Vec<(u32, PooledMsg<S>)>,
173	        pin_cores: &[usize],
174	        actor_loop: ActorLoopFn<S, R>,
175	    ) -> (Vec<Sender<SignalZC<S>>>, Vec<JoinHandle<R>>) {
176	        let actors = mgr.take_actors();
177	        let n = actors.len();
178	        let pool = self.pool.clone();
179	        let probe_name_prefix = mgr.probe_name_prefix().to_string();
180	
181	        let mut senders: Vec<Sender<SignalZC<S>>> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
182	        let mut receivers: Vec<Option<Receiver<SignalZC<S>>>> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
183	        for _ in 0..n {
184	            let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
185	            senders.push(tx);
186	            receivers.push(Some(rx));
187	        }
188	
189	        let mut handles: Vec<JoinHandle<R>> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
190	        for (id, actor) in actors.into_iter().enumerate() {
191	            #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
192	            // OK: receivers[id] was set to `Some(...)` in the loop above.
193	            let rx = receivers[id].take().unwrap();
194	            let peers: Vec<Sender<SignalZC<S>>> = senders.to_vec();
195	            let probe_name = format!("{}.actor{}", probe_name_prefix, id);
196	            let pin_target = if pin_cores.is_empty() {
197	                None
198	            } else {
199	                Some(pin_cores[id % pin_cores.len()])
200	            };
201	            let actor_pool = pool.clone();
202	            let h = thread::Builder::new()
203	                .name(format!("actor-zc-{id}"))
204	                .spawn(move || {
205	                    tprobe::pin::pin_current(pin_target);
206	                    actor_loop(actor, rx, peers, actor_pool, probe_name)
207	                })
208	                .expect("failed to spawn actor thread");
209	            handles.push(h);
210	        }
211	
212	        for (dst, msg) in initial_messages {
213	            #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
214	            // OK: receivers are alive (threads just spawned); a send
215	            //   failure indicates an immediate thread panic at startup
216	            //   which the join below surfaces with a clearer message.
217	            senders[dst as usize].send(SignalZC::User(msg)).unwrap();
218	        }
219	
220	        (senders, handles)
221	    }

225	    ///
226	    /// - Calls [`Self::spawn_and_seed`] to spawn threads and
227	    ///   deliver initial messages.
228	    /// - Sleeps `warmup`, sends `ClearCount` to every actor,
229	    ///   sleeps `measurement`, sends `Shutdown`, drops senders,

## Remove legacy run / run_probed / actor_loop_probed (0.6.0-6)

Deletes the all-in-one API that the lifecycle path replaced.
After this commit `RuntimeZC` exposes only `new` (inherent)
plus the [`Runtime`] trait surface (`startup` + `pool`).
The probe-instrumented per-thread loop and its function-
pointer scaffolding go with the legacy methods — probing
re-enters post-`0.6.0` via an actor-wrapper trait or
`TProbe::Counter` and will need its own per-thread loop
flavor when that work lands.

- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-5` → `0.6.0-6`.
- `crates/actor-x1/src/runtime_zc.rs`:
  - Removed `RuntimeZC::run` (probe-free all-in-one),
    `RuntimeZC::run_probed` (probed all-in-one), and the
    shared `RuntimeZC::run_inner` orchestrator.
  - Removed `actor_loop_probed` (per-thread probed loop)
    and the `ActorLoopFn<S, R>` type alias (only used to
    swap loops in `run_inner`).
  - Removed the `use tprobe::TProbe;` import (only
    consumer was `actor_loop_probed`).
  - Simplified `spawn_and_seed`: dropped the
    `<R: Send + 'static>` generic and the `actor_loop:
    ActorLoopFn<S, R>` parameter; hardcodes the call to
    `actor_loop::<S>` and returns
    `(Vec<Sender<SignalZC<S>>>, Vec<JoinHandle<u64>>)`
    concretely. Dropped the `probe_name_prefix` /
    `probe_name` plumbing (`actor_loop` no longer needs
    it).
  - Simplified `actor_loop`: dropped the `_probe_name`
    parameter (it only existed so the function pointer
    matched `ActorLoopFn`).
  - Module docstring collapsed from the two-style "API
    styles in this version" framing to a single
    "API surface (lifecycle-only since `0.6.0-6`)" list.
  - `SignalZC::ClearCount` doc trimmed: the legacy-
    probed-loop clause is gone. `Shutdown` doc now points
    at `Handle::stop` / `Handle::drop` (the only injectors
    left).
  - Removed three legacy tests:
    `ping_pong_runs_and_shuts_down`,
    `pool_is_full_after_shutdown`, `run_returns_counts`.
    Each exercised the legacy API; all three behaviors
    (drive traffic + drain invariant + per-actor counts)
    are covered by the lifecycle tests already in the
    module.
- `notes/todo.md`: mark `0.6.0-6` done.
- `notes/chores-03.md`: this section.

### Why drop the `spawn_and_seed` generic instead of keeping it

Keeping `spawn_and_seed<R>` "in case probed re-entry needs
it" speculatively re-introduces the same function-pointer
scaffolding the deletion just removed. Per VENDOR_A.md:
don't design for hypothetical future requirements. When
the wrapper-trait probed path lands, lifting `spawn_and_seed`
back to a generic is two minutes of work and the diff is
exactly recoverable from this commit's history. Keep
present code minimal.

### Why drop the legacy tests rather than rewrite them

The deleted tests asserted properties of the legacy API
(`run_probed` returns nonzero per-actor counts, `run`
returns counts, the legacy shutdown path drains the
pool). Rewriting them against the lifecycle API would
just duplicate the existing `lifecycle_*` tests — the
behaviors aren't legacy-specific, they're properties of
the actor loop and the drain invariant, which the
lifecycle tests already cover. Removing the tests
removes redundancy, not coverage.

### Smoke validation

- `cargo test`: 32 passed actor-x1 (35 in `0.6.0-5`, -3
  legacy tests removed) + 18 passed tprobe. All seven
  `lifecycle_*` tests pass.
- `cargo install --path crates/actor-x1` + `goalzc 0.5
  -w 0.2`: 226 K msg/s at 64 B unpinned. Normal range.
- The probed re-entry hook described in the chores
  ladder is not introduced here — it will land in a
  separate ladder post-`0.6.0`."}

{"file_path": "/home/<USER_1>/data/prgs/rust/actor-x1/crates/actor-x1/notes/lifecycle.md", "content": "# RuntimeZC lifecycle (0.6.0)

Reference for the zerocopy runtime's lifecycle API
([`crate::runtime_zc::Runtime`] +
[`crate::runtime_zc::Handle`]). The module rustdoc
([`runtime_zc`]) carries a runnable worked example; this
file carries the design rationale.

## Surface

- `pub trait Runtime<S: BufRefStore>` — `startup` (returns a
  `Handle<S>`), `pool` (borrows the underlying [`Pool<S>`]).
- `pub struct RuntimeZC<S>` — implements `Runtime<S>`; built
  via the inherent constructor `RuntimeZC::new(pool)`.
- `pub struct Handle<S>` — owned by the caller during the
  run; carries per-actor senders + join handles + a pool
  clone. Methods:
  - `run(duration)` — sleep a run window while actor threads
    process messages.
  - `reset_count()` — zero every actor's per-thread count.
  - `query_count() -> u64` — read the aggregate without
    stopping.
  - `pool() -> &Pool<S>` — accessor for post-startup
    `get_msg` / inspection.
  - `stop() -> u64` — graceful shutdown + join + aggregate.
  - `Drop` — silent graceful shutdown if `stop` was not
    called.

## Typical usage shape

- **Smoke / bin** (`goalzc`): one `startup`, one warmup
  `run`, `reset_count`, one measurement `run`, `stop`. The
  reported throughput excludes warmup. See
  `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goalzc.rs`.
- **Amortized bench** (`goalzc-crit`): one `startup` outside
  `b.iter_custom`, one warmup `run` outside the loop, then
  per criterion sample `reset_count` → `run(measurement)` →
  `query_count`. `stop` happens implicitly on `Drop` at the
  end of the bench function. See
  `crates/actor-x1/benches/goalzc-crit.rs`.

## Why a trait

- `pub trait Runtime<S>` exists so consumers reach through
  it (`use ...::Runtime;`) rather than the concrete type.
  The post-`0.6.0` ActorManager-driven graceful-shutdown
  work has a stable seam to drop into without rewriting
  consumer call sites.
- The trait is object-safe: `&self` / `&mut self`, no
  generic params on methods. A future `dyn Runtime<S>`
  consumer compiles without additional plumbing.
- Inherent `startup` / `pool` on `RuntimeZC` were dropped
  in `0.6.0-5` so the trait import is *required*. Without
  it, the call won't compile — the seam is enforced, not
  decorative.

## Why `Handle` is a concrete struct, not a trait

- Every runtime in scope today and short-horizon (the
  zerocopy family) shares the same handle shape: per-actor
  channel senders + per-actor `JoinHandle<u64>`. A trait
  here would add an associated type with no consumer
  needing the flexibility.
- Per VENDOR_A.md: don't design for hypothetical future
  requirements. If a second handle shape arrives (e.g.,
  the wrapper-trait probed path), lift `Handle` to an
  associated `type Handle: HandleApi<S>` on `Runtime`
  *then*. The diff is small and recoverable.

## Counter shape: per-thread `u64`, no atomics

- Each actor thread owns a local `u64`. The hot path
  (`actor_loop`) increments the local, no atomic ops, no
  shared memory writes.
- Aggregation happens at `stop` (sum over `JoinHandle::Output`)
  and at `query_count` (signal-and-reply, sum over received
  values).
- The bot thinks the cost rationale is the right one for
  the bench-shaped workload (ping-pong saturates a small
  number of cores, atomics on the count would dominate the
  per-message budget once `tprobe` is gone). Confirmed
  empirically across `0.5.0` (probed) and `0.6.0` (probe-
  free) — see `chores-02.md` / `chores-03.md` for the
  measured deltas.

## When to choose `query_count` vs `stop`

- `stop` — terminal. Sends `Shutdown`, joins all threads,
  returns the aggregate. Consumes the handle. Use for
  one-shot measurement runs.
- `query_count` — mid-flight. Sends `QueryCount(reply)` to
  each actor; each replies with its current local count
  and keeps running. Does *not* consume the handle. Use
  when the same actor mesh measures many windows in
  succession (amortized criterion benches; long-running
  smoke generators wanting periodic snapshots).
- Two successive `query_count` reads are monotonic non-
  decreasing but not equal — actors keep counting between
  calls.
- `query_count` is point-in-time, not a stop-the-world
  snapshot. Actors keep processing messages between the
  `QueryCount` send and the reply send (the signal is
  serialized with `User` messages in the per-actor
  channel). For amortized benchmarking this is exactly
  what's wanted: the reported count covers a wall-clock
  window that *contains* the `run(measurement)` window
  plus a small signal-handling delta.

## Why `reset_count` is explicit (no built-in warmup phase)

- The lifecycle API has no automatic warmup → measurement
  transition. The caller drives both windows with `run`
  and inserts `reset_count` at the boundary.
- This keeps `Handle::run(duration)` semantically simple
  (just "sleep `duration`, actors keep going") and avoids
  baking a warmup discipline into the API surface that
  not every consumer wants.
- The bot thinks the alternative (a `run(warmup, measure)`
  primitive) would over-specialize the API for the
  measurement use case at the expense of long-running
  smoke / interactive uses where there is no warmup phase.

## Why `Drop` is silent (panics swallowed)

- `Drop::drop` must not panic-during-drop (a double-panic
  aborts the process). The drop path sends `Shutdown` to
  each actor, joins, and discards both the per-thread
  counts and any join errors.
- Callers who care about actor-panic visibility must call
  `stop` explicitly — `stop` propagates panics via the
  unwrap on the join result. The chores-03 entry under
  `0.6.0-1` notes this contract; `goalzc-crit` relies on
  it (drops the handle at end-of-bench, silently).

## Best-effort `reset_count` / `query_count` semantics

- Both methods iterate over the handle's senders and send
  their signal best-effort: a closed channel (actor thread
  already exited) is silently skipped.
- For `reset_count`, the skipped actor's count is captured
  by its `JoinHandle::Output` and rolled into `stop`'s
  total — nothing is lost.
- For `query_count`, the implementation tracks how many
  sends succeeded and only `recv`s that many replies, so a
  dead thread can't deadlock the caller. In practice, the
  handle is alive (<USER_2>`stop`) so all sends succeed; the
  defensive shape is for symmetry with `reset_count`.

## Drain invariant

- By the time the handle's drop / `stop` completes, every
  `PooledMsg` ever in flight has been dropped, so
  `pool.free_len() == pool.size()`.
- Every lifecycle test in `runtime_zc.rs` asserts this
  after the run. It's the single property that says "the
  shutdown was clean" — buffers that didn't make it back
  to the pool would indicate a leaked message, a wedged
  thread, or a contract violation in `ActorZC`.

## What's intentionally *not* on the lifecycle surface

- **Per-message latency stats / band-table.** Probing left
  the runtime in `0.6.0-2`; the legacy probed loop and
  scaffolding were removed in `0.6.0-6`. Probing re-enters
  in a separate ladder (post-`0.6.0`) via an actor-wrapper
  trait or `TProbe::Counter` — neither will live on the
  `Runtime` trait itself. The bot thinks the right home
  is a wrapper that consumes an `ActorZC` and exposes the
  same trait + a probe accessor; the runtime stays
  unaware.
- **Per-actor count breakdown.** `stop` returns the
  aggregate; per-actor counts are not exposed today.
  Trivially recoverable later (change `stop`'s return to
  `Vec<u64>` or add a sibling method); not done because
  no consumer needs it yet.
- **Typed messages to the runtime.** The lifecycle uses
  internal `SignalZC` variants only; there is no public
  channel for callers to push typed control messages.
  The post-`0.6.0` ActorManager-driven graceful-shutdown
  work is expected to introduce this.

## History

- `0.6.0-0` — plan marker. `chores-03.md`.
- `0.6.0-1` — `Handle` + `startup` / `run` / `stop`.
- `0.6.0-2` — `reset_count`; `goalzc` / `goalzc-crit` move
  to the lifecycle; probing leaves the runtime.
- `0.6.0-3` — shared `report` module (side-refactor).
- `0.6.0-4` — `query_count` + amortized `goalzc-crit`.
- `0.6.0-5` — `pub trait Runtime<S>` + inherent
  `startup` / `pool` removed; `ClearProbe → ClearCount`.
- `0.6.0-6` — legacy `run` / `run_probed` /
  `actor_loop_probed` removed; module is lifecycle-only.
- `0.6.0` — close: this notes file + worked example in
  the module rustdoc.
"}

1	# Notes
2	
3	See [design.md](../crates/actor-x1/notes/design.md)
4	
5	
6	## jj tips
7	
8	For users new to jj see [jj-tips.md](jj-tips.md).
9	
10	```
11	## Chores format
12	
13	Filename: "chores-XX.md"
14	example: chores-01.md
15	
16	Format of section labels: "## <short description> (X.Y.Z)"
17	example: "## Topic format description (0.1.0)"
18	
19	Example chore file:
20	```
21	# Chores-01.md
22	 
23	General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
24	more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
25	how and why of a particular chore.
26	
27	## Do something (1.3.1)
28	
29	Describe something
30	```
31	
32	## Versioning during development
33	
34	This is using jujustiu, jj + git and we'll see how it goes. Below is my
35	git workflow, jj will be different but we'll have to discover that as
36	we go.
37	
38	Every plan must start with a version bump. Choose the approach based on scope:
39	
40	- **Single-step** (recommended for mechanical/focused changes): bump directly to
41	  `X.Y.Z`, implement in one commit. Simpler history.
42	- **Multi-step** (for exploratory/large changes): bump to `X.Y.Z-devN`, implement
43	  across multiple commits, final commit removes `-devN`.
44	
45	The plan should recommend one approach and get user approval before starting.
46	
47	For multi-step:
48	1. Bump version to `X.Y.Z-devN` with a plan and commit as a chore marker
49	2. Implement in one or more `-devN` commits (bump N as needed)
50	3. Final commit removes `-devN`, updates todo/chores — this is the "done" marker
51	
52	The final release commit (without `-devN`) signals completion rather than amending
53	prior commits. This keeps the git history readable and makes it easy to see which
54	commits were exploratory vs final.
55	
56	## Todo format
57	
58	Todo.md contains two main sections "Todo" and "Done" each item is a
59	short explanations of a tasks and links to more details using 1 or more
60	references.
61	
62	Multiple references must be separated: `[2],[3]` not `[2,3]` or `[2][3]`.
63	In markdown, `[2,3]` is a single ref key (won't resolve) and `[2][3]`
64	is parsed as display text `2` with ref key `3` (so `[2]` won't resolve).
65	
66	Examples:
67	
68	# Todo
69	
70	- Add new feature X [details](chores-01.md#feature-x)
71	- Fix bug Y [1]
72	
73	# Done
74	
75	- Fixed issue Z [2],[3]
76	
77	[1]: chores-01bugs.md#bug-y

46	- **Bound `TProbe`'s records-buffer memory.** Each scope

49	  buffers 260M records ≈ 8 GB minimum, ~16 GB after

51	  typical dev boxes. Pre-existing from 0.1.0-2 when the
52	  probe was vendored; becomes hard to miss at long

57	    dropped counter and skip the `push`. Report shows

59	    cost. Partial data on very long runs.
60	  - (b) **Periodic inline drain.** When records hit a
61	    threshold, drain into the histogram and continue.
62	    Memory bounded. Adds occasional drain stalls (ms-ish)
63	    that show up in the `p99-max` tail.
64	  - (c) **Inline drain, no buffer.** `end` / `end_batch`

67	    to the hot path — non-trivial when the probe is

1	# Chores-03.md
2	
3	Chores for the `0.6.0` ladder onward.
4	
5	## RuntimeZC lifecycle: startup / run / stop — plan marker (0.6.0-0)
6	
7	Plan marker for the `0.6.0` multi-step ladder. Splits the
8	runtime's all-in-one `run` / `run_probed` into a caller-
9	orchestrated lifecycle (`startup` / `Handle::run` /
10	`Handle::stop`). Probe support leaves the runtime entirely;
11	re-enters later via `TProbe::Counter` or an actor-wrapper
12	trait (out of scope for this ladder). `stop` is the
13	explicit graceful primitive, matching the post-`0.6.0`
14	typed-message-to-runtime story.
15	
16	### Shape
17	
18	```
19	let handle = rt.startup(&mut mgr, initial, pin_cores);
20	handle.run(duration);        // optional, repeatable
21	let total = handle.stop();   // u64 aggregate; sends Shutdown
22	```
23	
24	### Multi-step ladder
25	
26	(Revised mid-flight after `0.6.0-1`. Original ladder had
27	three sub-steps; expanded to five to make the trait
28	introduction and amortized-bench work explicit. Revised
29	again after `0.6.0-2` to insert the shared-`report`-module
30	side-refactor as `0.6.0-3`, shifting the lifecycle work
31	that was -3/-4/-5 to -4/-5/-6.)
32	
33	- `0.6.0-0` — plan marker (this section + version bump).
34	- `0.6.0-1` — `Handle` + `RuntimeZC::startup` /
35	  `Handle::run` / `Handle::stop`; tests updated. Existing
36	  `run` / `run_probed` stay alongside (additive step).
37	- `0.6.0-2` — Migrate `goalzc` bin and `goalzc-crit` bench
38	  to the lifecycle API. New `Handle::reset_count` (sends
39	  `ClearProbe`; each actor thread zeros its per-thread
40	  count on receipt). `--warmup` restored on `goalzc` and
41	  in `goalzc-crit`'s warmup → measurement split. `goalzc`
42	  loses its band-table (no probing); keeps the msg/s line
43	  as a smoke generator.
44	- `0.6.0-3` — Shared `actor_x1::report` module. Extracts
45	  the bin-prelude helpers duplicated across `goal1` /
46	  `goal2` / `goalzc` (parser, banner, apparatus line,
47	  pinning line) into a single home so the upcoming
48	  probing-re-enters work (post-`0.6.0`, when a probed
49	  `goalzc_probed` bin lands on the wrapper-trait probe
50	  path) has a clean shared surface to call into instead
51	  of yet another copy.
52	- `0.6.0-4` — `Handle::query_count` via signal-and-reply
53	  (oneshot per thread). `goalzc-crit` goes amortized:
54	  `startup` once / `reset_count → run(duration) →
55	  query_count` per criterion sample. Reports the new
56	  amortized number; bench-vs-bin gap collapses (or
57	  doesn't, and we learn something).
58	- `0.6.0-5` — Introduce `Runtime` trait. `RuntimeZC` impls
59	  it. `goalzc` / `goalzc-crit` / tests reach through the
60	  trait, not the concrete type. `SignalZC::ClearProbe`
61	  renamed to `ClearCount` (probe is gone).
62	- `0.6.0-6` — Remove legacy `run` / `run_probed` /
63	  `actor_loop_probed`. Runtime is probe-free +
64	  lifecycle-only.
65	- `0.6.0` — close.
66	
67	### Decisions locked in
68	
69	- **Counter**: per-thread local `u64`, no atomics. Returned
70	  via `JoinHandle` at `stop`. `stop -> u64` aggregate. KIS;
71	  per-actor breakdown is a future `TProbe::Counter`
72	  concern.
73	- **`Handle::run(duration) -> ()`** — just sleeps for the
74	  run window. Counts not readable mid-flight by design.
75	- **`Handle::Drop`** calls `stop` if forgotten; result is
76	  discarded. Join errors are swallowed (drop must not
77	  panic-during-drop).
78	- **Probing leaves the runtime.** `goalzc`'s band-table
79	  goes with it. Probe re-introduction is post-`0.6.0`
80	  work, via `TProbe::Counter` or an actor-wrapper trait.
81	- **`Runtime` trait** introduced in `0.6.0-4`. Consumers
82	  reach through the trait so the post-`0.6.0`
83	  ActorManager-driven graceful shutdown work has a clean
84	  seam to drop into.
85	
86	### Defaults that aren't yet locked
87	
88	- `Handle::pool()` accessor so the caller can inject ad-hoc
89	  messages post-startup. Default yes; revisit during
90	  `0.6.0-1` if the API gets ugly.
91	
92	### Naming: teardown → stop
93	
94	The `0.5.0` close section's "What's next" pointer used
95	the name `teardown` for the lifecycle's shutdown
96	primitive. During the `0.6.0-0` planning round the name
97	settled on `stop` — matches the post-`0.6.0` typed-
98	message-to-runtime story. The chores-02 mention of
99	`teardown` is historical (accurate to the moment it was
100	written, pre-rename) and is left in place per the same
101	precedent `0.5.1` set with `run_no_probe → run`.
102	
103	## Handle + RuntimeZC::startup / Handle::run / Handle::stop (0.6.0-1)
104	
105	Adds the lifecycle API alongside the existing all-in-one
106	`run` / `run_probed`. Caller drives the actor mesh through
107	[`startup`] → [`Handle::run`] (any number of windows) →
108	[`Handle::stop`] (returns the aggregate `u64` count and
109	joins). Probe-free; counts come from per-thread local
110	`u64`s summed via `JoinHandle` at `stop`. The all-in-one
111	paths still work (refactored to share spawn / seed logic);
112	they go away in `0.6.0-3`.
113	
114	- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-0` → `0.6.0-1`.
115	- `crates/actor-x1/src/runtime_zc.rs`:
116	  - New private `RuntimeZC::spawn_and_seed<R>` extracts
117	    the spawn + channel-wire + initial-message-deliver
118	    logic shared by the all-in-one `run_inner` and the
119	    new `startup`. `run_inner` is now a thin wrapper that
120	    composes `spawn_and_seed` with the warmup / clear /
121	    measurement / shutdown / join sequence.
122	  - New `pub fn RuntimeZC::startup(mgr, initial, pin) ->
123	    Handle<S>` returns a live handle to the actor mesh.
124	  - New `pub struct Handle<S = MutexLifo>` with
125	    `pub fn run(&self, window: Duration)` (just sleeps),
126	    `pub fn pool(&self) -> &Pool<S>` (caller injection /
127	    inspection), `pub fn stop(self) -> u64` (sends
128	    `Shutdown`, joins, sums per-thread counts — panics
129	    on actor panic).
130	  - `impl Drop for Handle` performs silent graceful
131	    shutdown if `stop` was not called: sends `Shutdown`,
132	    joins, swallows panics and counts. Drop must not
133	    panic-during-drop.
134	  - Module-level docstring: rewritten around the two API
135	    styles (Lifecycle preferred / All-in-one legacy).
136	  - Tests: `lifecycle_round_trip_returns_total`,
137	    `lifecycle_multiple_run_windows_accumulate`,
138	    `lifecycle_handle_pool_accessor`,
139	    `lifecycle_handle_drop_shuts_down_cleanly`. All four
140	    validate the drain invariant (`pool.free_len() ==
141	    pool.size()` after the handle goes away).
142	- `notes/todo.md`: mark `0.6.0-1` done.
143	- `notes/chores-03.md`: this section.
144	
145	### Design notes
146	
147	- **`Handle`'s state**: `senders: Option<Vec<Sender<...>>>`
148	  and `handles: Option<Vec<JoinHandle<u64>>>`. `stop`
149	  consumes via `take()`; `Drop` checks the same `Option`s
150	  and runs the silent path only if `stop` didn't.
151	  Simpler than typestate; KIS.
152	- **Counter aggregation**: each actor thread keeps a
153	  local `u64`, returned via `JoinHandle::Output`. `stop`
154	  sums them with `saturating_add`. No atomics in the hot
155	  path.
156	- **No mid-flight count read**: `Handle::run(window)`
157	  returns `()`. Per-window deltas would require atomics
158	  or signal-and-reply; both rejected as not worth the
159	  complexity at the user's KIS preference.
160	- **`spawn_and_seed` lives on `RuntimeZC`**, not as a
161	  free function, because it uses `self.pool` and is the
162	  natural place for the shared logic. Generic over `R`
163	  so both probe-free and probed actor loops share it.
164	- **Pool sizing in tests**: the lifecycle tests use the
165	  `Pool::new(., 4)` ping-pong-steady-state recommendation
166	  from the `0.5.0` chores (4 buffers covers 2 in flight
167	  + 2 headroom). One initial test draft used the
168	  capacity-2 pool from a non-running test and hit
169	  `NoMsgs` under traffic; standardized on 4.
170	
171	### What's not in 0.6.0-1
172	
173	- `goalzc` and `goalzc-crit` still call the legacy
174	  `run_probed` / `run` paths. `0.6.0-2` migrates them.
175	- Legacy `RuntimeZC::run` / `run_probed` /
176	  `actor_loop_probed` / the `ClearProbe` signal path stay
177	  untouched for now. `0.6.0-3` removes them.
178	
179	## Migrate goalzc bin and goalzc-crit bench to lifecycle (0.6.0-2)
180	
181	`goalzc` and `goalzc-crit` move off the legacy all-in-one
182	`RuntimeZC::run_probed` / `run` to the lifecycle API
183	(`startup` / `Handle::run` / `Handle::stop`). Adds
184	`Handle::reset_count` so the warmup → measurement
185	boundary can zero per-thread counts mid-flight. `goalzc`
186	loses its band-table report (no probing in the runtime;
187	re-enters post-`0.6.0`) and becomes a smoke generator
188	that prints msg/s. `goalzc-crit` keeps its
189	cycle-per-sample shape, just through the new API.
190	
191	- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-1` → `0.6.0-2`.
192	- `crates/actor-x1/src/runtime_zc.rs`:
193	  - New `pub fn Handle::reset_count(&self)` sends
194	    `SignalZC::ClearProbe` to every actor thread; on
195	    receipt each thread zeros its per-thread count.
196	    Best-effort: if a thread already exited, the send
197	    silently fails (its count is already captured in
198	    its `JoinHandle::Output`).
199	  - New test `lifecycle_reset_count_runs_clean` exercises
200	    `startup → run → reset_count → run → stop`; asserts
201	    nonzero post-reset total + drain invariant.
202	- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goalzc.rs`:
203	  - CLI: drop `--ticks` (`-t`), `--decimals` (`-d`).
204	    Keep `duration_s` (positional), `--warmup` (`-w`,
205	    default 0.5), `--size` (`-s`), `--pin` (`-p`).
206	  - Drop the apparatus calibration call and the
207	    per-thread `tprobe` band-table report.
208	  - Use `rt.startup` → `handle.run(warmup)` →
209	    `handle.reset_count()` → `handle.run(measurement)`
210	    → `handle.stop` to drive the actors.
211	  - Output: version banner, throughput line
212	    (`goalzc: <count> messages in <Ds> (<R> M msg/s,
213	    <N> actors, size=<S> B)`), and `pinning:` line if
214	    `--pin` was set. No `apparatus:` line, no band
215	    table.
216	  - Imports trimmed: `tprobe::{fmt_commas, pin}` only
217	    (was `tprobe::{self as perf, fmt_commas, pin,
218	    ticks}` plus probe-side report calls).
219	  - `n_actors = 2` hardcoded since the bin always
220	    creates two actors (assertion already pins
221	    `(a_id, b_id) == (0, 1)`).
222	- `crates/actor-x1/benches/goalzc-crit.rs`:
223	  - Switch `rt.run` → `rt.startup` /
224	    `handle.run(warmup)` / `handle.reset_count()` /
225	    `handle.run(measurement)` / `handle.stop`.
226	  - Keep the prior 50 ms warmup + 100 ms measurement
227	    split. `per_msg_ns = measurement / measurement_count`
228	    (post-reset only).
229	  - Module docstring rewritten around the lifecycle
230	    API and the smoke-bench scope.
231	- `notes/todo.md`: mark `0.6.0-2` done.
232	- `notes/chores-03.md`: this section.
233	
234	### Smoke results (`--size 64`, unpinned)
235	
236	- `goalzc-crit/pingpong`: ~260 K msg/s (criterion CI
237	  [250, 269] K elem/s; "Performance has improved",
238	  p=0.04 vs the pre-restoration single-window baseline
239	  at ~233 K). Restoring `--warmup` (50 ms) before the
240	  100 ms measurement window — and using `reset_count`
241	  to drop the warmup count — exposes the steady-state
242	  rate.
243	- `goalzc 10 -w 3`: ~293 K msg/s. Modest improvement vs
244	  the <USER_2>`0.6.0` probed path (~281 K); the bot thinks
245	  this is the probe overhead leaving the hot loop —
246	  ~5.8 ns / dispatch ≈ 0.17% of the per-message cost —
247	  near the edge of run-to-run noise but pointing the
248	  right way.
249	- Bench-vs-bin ratio: 260 / 293 ≈ 0.89, narrower than
250	  the pre-restoration 232 / 281 ≈ 0.83. The remaining
251	  11% is the per-sample fresh-`startup` cost in the
252	  bench; `0.6.0-3`'s `startup`-once + `query_count`
253	  amortization aims at that.
254	
255	### CLI breaking change in 0.6.0-2
256	
257	`goalzc`'s `--ticks` / `--decimals` flags are gone (band-
258	table is gone). `--warmup` is preserved with the same
259	semantics it had <USER_2>`0.6.0`: warmup window precedes
260	measurement, and reported throughput reflects only the
261	measurement window.
262	
263	### Naming: window → duration
264	
265	`Handle::run`'s parameter `window: Duration` renamed to
266	`duration: Duration` — matches `std::thread::sleep(dur)`
267	and `tokio::time::sleep(duration)` conventions, removes
268	the overloaded "window" reading from the public API. In
269	prose, bare "window" becomes "run window"; "warmup
270	window" / "measurement window" stay as already-qualified
271	compound terms. The `0.6.0-1` chores section above
272	describes the parameter as `window: Duration`, accurate
273	at the time, left in place per the same precedent
274	`0.5.1` set with `run_no_probe → run`.
275	
276	## Shared `report` module: extract bin-prelude helpers (0.6.0-3)
277	
278	Side-refactor inserted into the `0.6.0` ladder between the
279	lifecycle migration (`0.6.0-2`) and the upcoming
280	`query_count` work (`0.6.0-4`). Collapses the prelude
281	helpers that `goal1` / `goal2` / `goalzc` each had a copy
282	of into a single `actor_x1::report` module. No behavior
283	change — output is byte-for-byte identical across all three
284	bins.
285	
286	Motivation:
287	
288	- The bot thinks the post-`0.6.0` probing-re-enters work
289	  (when `goalzc_probed` lands on the wrapper-trait / 
290	  `TProbe::Counter` path) will want the same prelude lines
291	  as `goal1` / `goal2`. Doing the dedup *before* that bin
292	  arrives means one shared surface to call into instead
293	  of a fourth copy.
294	- `goal1` and `goal2` each duplicated the
295	  `parse_non_negative_secs` clap helper, the
296	  `framing / loop_per_iter / per-event` apparatus
297	  printout, and the `pinning:` line; `goalzc` had the
298	  parser and the multi-actor pinning printout.
299	
300	Edits:
301	
302	- `crates/actor-x1/Cargo.toml`: `0.6.0-2` → `0.6.0-3`.
303	- `crates/actor-x1/src/lib.rs`: declare `pub mod report;`.
304	- `crates/actor-x1/src/report.rs`: new module.
305	  - `parse_non_negative_secs(s) -> Result<f64, String>` —
306	    clap `value_parser` for non-negative finite seconds.
307	  - `parse_pin_cores(spec: Option<&str>) -> Vec<usize>` —
308	    `None` → `vec![]`; bad input prints
309	    `error: --pin: <msg>` and exits `2`. Centralizing the
310	    exit here keeps each bin free of duplicated error
311	    handling.
312	  - `print_banner()` — `actor-x1 <version>` one-liner from
313	    this crate's `CARGO_PKG_*`.
314	  - `print_apparatus(&Overhead, inner: u64)` — the
315	    `apparatus: framing=... ; loop_per_iter=... ; per-event
316	    at inner=N = ...` line.
317	  - `print_pinning(&[usize], n_actors: usize)` — multi-actor
318	    `pinning:` line (goal2 / goalzc wording —
319	    `actor<i>→core<n>`).
320	  - `print_pinning_main(Option<usize>)` — single-thread
321	    `pinning:` line (goal1 wording — `main → core <c>`).
322	    Distinct from `print_pinning` because goal1 pins the
323	    main thread itself, not a spawned actor; the prior
324	    output preserved both forms verbatim.
325	- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goal1.rs`: strip duplicated
326	  helpers; call `report::print_banner`,
327	  `report::parse_pin_cores`, `report::print_pinning_main`,
328	  `report::print_apparatus`. `parse_non_negative_secs`
329	  flag bodies now reference `report::parse_non_negative_secs`.
330	  Tprobe import trimmed: `tprobe::{self as perf, fmt_commas,
331	  pin}` (drops `ticks` — the per-event ns conversion lives
332	  in `report` now).
333	- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goal2.rs`: same shape.
334	  `parse_pin_cores` collapses the `match cli.pin.as_deref()
335	  { ... pin::parse_cores ... exit(2) }` block to one line.
336	  Tprobe import trimmed: `tprobe::{self as perf, fmt_commas}`
337	  (drops `pin` and `ticks` — goal2 doesn't pin the main
338	  thread, only spawned actors via the runtime).
339	- `crates/actor-x1/src/bin/goalzc.rs`: same shape, smaller
340	  surface (no apparatus call; no probing). Local
341	  `parse_positive_size` for `--size` stays in the bin —
342	  only goalzc has a payload-size flag, so it doesn't belong
343	  in the shared module. Tprobe import trimmed: `tprobe::
344	  fmt_commas` (drops `pin` — `parse_pin_cores` covers the
345	  one call site).
346	- `notes/todo.md`: insert `0.6.0-3` done line; renumber the
347	  lifecycle steps that were -3/-4/-5 to -4/-5/-6.
348	- `notes/chores-03.md`: revise the ladder table; this
349	  section.
350	
351	### Why the helpers live in `actor-x1`, not `tprobe`
352	
353	- The formatted lines are *bin prelude*, not perf-library
354	  surface. `tprobe` already owns the data
355	  ([`Overhead`], `ticks_per_ns`, `fmt_commas`); the bins
356	  own the *wording* (column spacing, label choice,
357	  pinning prose). Keeping the wording in `actor-x1` puts
358	  the prose next to the bins that produce it.
359	- A future external consumer of `tprobe` would print the
360	  same numbers in its own house style; promoting our
361	  particular phrasing to `tprobe` would foist our prose
362	  on every downstream <USER_3>
363	
364	### Why two pinning helpers
365	
366	`goal1` pins the main thread itself (single-threaded) and
367	its line says `pinning: main → core <c>`; `goal2` /
368	`goalzc` pin spawned actor threads and their line says
369	`pinning: actor<i>→core<n>`. The two are intentionally
370	worded differently (`main` vs `actor<i>`; spaced `→` vs
371	unspaced `→`). Preserving byte-for-byte output across the
372	refactor meant providing both forms rather than collapsing
373	them.
374	
375	### Bin-output policy left in the bins
376	
377	- `--ticks` / `--decimals` flags (probed bins only).
378	- The per-actor `probe.report(...)` call (each bin chooses
379	  which probes to render).
380	- The throughput line (`goal1: ... messages in ...`) — the
381	  bin name is baked into the format string. Promoting that
382	  to `report::print_throughput(&str, count, dur_s, ...)`
383	  would gain little and lose the literal-grep-ability of
384	  the per-bin line.

2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Actor-x1 is a system that uses Communicating
6	Sequential Process (CSP) invented by Tony Hoare
7	In 1978 and is commonly termed the actor model.
8	
9	 - There will be a management system (MS) that:
10	
11	   - Provides the capability to interact with
12	     the runtime providing control and to capture
13	     logs and assists in developing the app
14	   - Creates an hello world scaffolding
15	   - provides discovery capabilities of other
16	     other actors.
17	
18	 - A runtime that drives the system and provides
19	   resources and services for the system
20	   - interfaces between the manager and the application
21	 
22	 - One or more actors running on one or more
23	   threads. Each actor adheres to these
24	   invariants:
25	   - Has on basic entry point; handler()
26	   - The handler() handles one message at a time and
27	     must run to completion as quickly as possible.
28	   - The handler() never ever blocks
29	   - If a handler() has tasks that take to much time
30	     a technique that can be used is to spawn
31	     threads to do work. That thread would then use
32	     messages to communicate with its parent and
33	     other actors as it does its work.
34

37	     This potentially allows an Actor to implement
38	     sophisticated algorithms and prove correct operation.
